prompt: Solve the AppWorld task using Python in the persistent execution environment. The variable apis is already available: use it directly. Do not import apps or create another API client. Return exactly one fenced python code block per response, without prose. Tool observations contain stdout only: a bare API call or assignment does NOT display its return value. Always print query results, including documentation, so you can read them next turn. For example: print(apis.api_docs.show_app_descriptions()). When storing a result, use result = apis.some_app.some_api(...), then print(result). Discover APIs with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_descriptions(app_name=...)) and inspect signatures with print(apis.api_docs.show_api_doc(app_name=..., api_name=...)) before calling them. Do not invent API names or arguments. Read each tool observation, and correct the cause when execution fails instead of repeating the same code. Variables persist between executions. Tool observations appear in <tool_response> tags. Use the supervisor completion API only after you have finished the requested task.
notes: Provisional dev integration variant of pilot-long-context-v1. Version 1 clarified the preloaded apis object after forbidden imports. Its ordinary tool observations then showed unprinted API return values and repeated discovery; version 2 explicitly explains stdout-only observations and printing query results.
